# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot identify any wire contents by touch, and the display, light, and engraved marking provide me no usable information. I need Mute to provide the manual’s rule and establish a visual code with Deaf so Deaf can report the required wire position through Mute. I will not cut until a wire number is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel no wire markings or other usable clues. Please tell me the exact manual rule, and establish with Deaf a code for reporting the required wire position: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, and OK means wire 3. Have Deaf send that report; then tell me the wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light is off. Plate is engraved question mark. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute sent gestures: one thumbs-up, then two victory signs, then three OK signs. Use the manual to determine the required action.

The bomb information relayed from Deaf is: display 0, light off, plate marked with a question mark, and wire colors red, blue, green in positions 1–3. However, I cannot see Mute’s gestures, so the thumbs-up, victory signs, and OK signs convey nothing to me. I still do not have the manual rule or a confirmed required wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Please speak the manual rule plainly, and have Deaf report the required wire position to you in words; then tell me the position.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gestures, in order: one thumbs-up, then one thumbs-down, then one OK sign. Bomb remains display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red blue green.

The latest three gestures still do not tell me which wire is required: I cannot see them, and no shared meaning for that sequence has been established. I will set a precise protocol through Mute: Mute should compute the answer from the manual and send exactly one gesture—👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, or 👌 for wire 3. Deaf can then report that single gesture to me in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the manual to compute the required wire. On your next turn, send exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, OK means wire 3. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures are, in order: thumbs-up, thumbs-down, OK, then handshake. Bomb remains display 0, light off, plate ?, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The reported gestures are still ambiguous because no agreed code has been followed, and the manual’s rule remains unknown to me. Since Mute cannot speak, I need Deaf to act as the relay: Mute should gesture the manual’s complete instruction or answer using a clearly stated, repeated code. I will not risk cutting based on the four gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf can see your gestures and speak to me next turn. Ignore all earlier codes: send exactly one symbol only—👍 for required wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, or 👌 for wire 3. If none applies, send ✋. Deaf, please report that one symbol in words next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gesture is one handshake. Bomb remains display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The handshake is not one of the three wire-code gestures I specified, so it does not identify a wire. I will treat it only as an acknowledgment and request the answer again with a single unambiguous symbol. I still have not received the manual rule or a valid wire number, so cutting would be unsafe.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Handshake is not a wire answer. Next turn send exactly one gesture and nothing else: thumbs-up means cut wire 1; thumbs-down means cut wire 2; OK means cut wire 3. Deaf will report which one you sent.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New gesture from Mute: raised hand, palm out. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red blue green.

The raised palm is not a valid answer under the wire code, so the required wire is still unknown. I will simplify the protocol further: Mute should send only repeated thumbs-up gestures, with the count equal to the wire position—one for wire 1, two for wire 2, or three for wire 3. Deaf should relay that count in words. I will not cut on the invalid palm signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please ignore every earlier gesture code. Send only thumbs-up gestures: exactly one means wire 1, exactly two means wire 2, exactly three means wire 3. Deaf, report only the number of thumbs-up gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꗃ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New gesture from Mute: thumbs-up. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

Mute’s single thumbs-up matches the latest agreed code: one thumbs-up means wire 1. Deaf has relayed that the bomb remains unchanged, so I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
